question: Who founded the Servants of India Society?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the ‘Servants of India Society.

 
 
• It was formed in Pune, Maharashtra in 1905.
 
 
 
• **Gokhale left the Deccan **Education Society to form this association.
 
• This association was** formed with a small group **of educated Indians.
 
• To **promote social and human development** and overthrow British rule in India was the objective of forming this association.
 
• The organization promoted many campaigns for education, sanitation, and healthcare.
 
• **Untouchability, discrimination, alcoholism, poverty, and oppression of women issues were raised.**
 
• **Hitavada was the magazine**, which was published through the association.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian National Congress

 
 
• On December 28, 1885, the Indian National Congress was founded in Bombay by Scottish resident Alan Octavian Hume. Hence, Option 4 is correct.
 
• Allan Octavian Hume was a British member of the Imperial Civil Service and one of the founders of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He also founded the journal Stray Feathers in which he and his subscribers recorded notes on birds from across India.
 
• He left India in 1894 and found the South London Botanical Institute towards the end of his life.
 
• List of the Birds of India, My Scrap Book: Or Rough Notes on Indian Oology and Ornithology, and Hints on Esoteric Theosophy are his important works.
 
• The first president of the Congress was Vyomesh Chandra Banerjee.
 
• The youngest president of the Congress was Abdul Kalam Azad, who presided over the special session of Delhi in 1925.
 
• The 1888 session of the Congress was presided over by the first Englishman George Yule.
 
• Motilal Nehru presided over the 1919 Amritsar session of the Congress.
 
 
 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati**
 
 
• **​**A religious leader and founder of the Arya Samaj, a socio-religious reform movement
 
• His ideas were accessible to the people of Northern India through the use of Hindi. 
 
• He believed that the practices of many religions and communities, such as idol worship, animal sacrifice, and child marriage, were contrary to the wisdom of the Vedas.
 
• His political message was "India for the Indians
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**
 
 
• **​**A political thinker and activist who was involved in the Boycott and Swadeshi movement
 
• He condemned the British efforts to control the Bubonic plague in Bombay and was sentenced to 18 months in prison.
 
• He started the Boycott and Swadeshi movement to boycott Western goods and use Indian-produced goods and services
 
 
 
• **Jyotirao Phule**
 
 
• His work focused on women's rights, child rights, caste politics, literacy, and eradicating superstition.
